context.exploration_scope: Connected PHASE-SSI-S9's operationally-ready Principle to the real SSI flow as a change-gated trigger: compared the last known real state (through S9) against a fresh read of the same real files, and only performed a Principle-vs-independent comparison if an actual change was found

problem: A Principle that re-evaluates on every run regardless of whether anything real changed is not being applied to real application flow, it is just being re-asserted -- connecting it correctly required a real change-detection gate, checked against the actual current state of the same real files this automation has been reading since S5, not a standing always-on re-check.

decision.decision_summary: No real state change detected since PHASE-SSI-S9 (chain_status, gpu_available, and hold_status all unchanged) -- correctly ended without performing any Principle-vs-independent comparison.

action.action_summary: Compared the last known real state (recorded through S9) against a fresh read of the real trace chain and PRODUCTION_VALIDATION_HOLD.json; gated all further comparison strictly on an actual detected change; on change, computed the independent judgment before the Principle-guided judgment and compared them; never wrote to the real chain/hold files.

result.note: Correctly reported NO_REAL_TRIGGER -- the Principle is connected to the real flow but stayed inert because nothing real actually changed, which is the intended change-gated behavior, not a failure.

cause.root_cause_summary: Wiring a validated Principle into a real flow without a real change gate would make every run re-litigate the same already-settled state -- the gate is what keeps "connected to the real operational flow" from silently meaning "runs a no-op comparison every time," and what makes an eventual real trigger meaningful rather than routine.

lesson: Connecting a Principle to a real operational flow is only meaningfully different from testing it in isolation if the connection includes an honest gate on whether anything real actually changed -- reporting NO_REAL_TRIGGER when nothing changed is the correct, non-lazy answer, not a shortcut past doing the check.
